releases.name: FreeWallet 2.1.2
releases.notes:
The first release signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Gatekeeper opens it without the Open Anyway steps. Apple Silicon only.

- The application is signed with the hardened runtime. NW.js needs two entitlements under it, `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` and `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`, which are applied to the main executable and to each helper application.
- After a page reload, bitcore loads again instead of failing with "More than one instance of bitcore-lib found", which left key derivation broken until the application was restarted.
- Asset artwork, audio and video fall back to the first listed entry when the preferred formats are missing. Before, the fallback produced nothing.

releases.name: Squint 0.9.8
releases.notes:
Remove Location Data now removes data hidden after the loop count or colour profile in a GIF, and in a TIFF directory that only the Exif directory links to. It refuses a HEIC or AVIF whose item index sits outside its metadata box or lists an item twice, and a GIF whose colour profile is malformed.

The engine also gains seven safety lints, enforced in CI, and two fixes: the buffer returned over the C interface is now freed the way it was allocated, and encoding an image whose pixel count disagrees with its size returns an error instead of reading past the buffer.

releases.name: Squint 0.9.5
releases.notes:
Remove Location Data now cleans a raw file's embedded preview instead of refusing the file.

Raw previews. A raw file carries an embedded preview, a JPEG with metadata of its own: an iPhone ProRAW file's preview keeps the GPS position, the phone, the lens and the capture time. 0.9.4 refused such a file. Its preview is now cleaned where it lies: the EXIF keeps only the orientation the preview is shown by, the XMP, comments and other metadata segments are zeroed, and nothing in the file moves. An HDR gain map in the preview keeps its rendering parameters, under the rule Remove Location Data already applies to a photograph's gain map, so the preview keeps its HDR. iPhone ProRAW and Ricoh GR II files now strip.

If you stripped iPhone ProRAW or other raw files with Squint 0.9.3 or earlier, strip them again: those versions reported them clean while their previews still held the location.

Still refused: a preview whose gain map's XMP holds more than its rendering parameters, with the message "this file's embedded preview has a gain map whose XMP holds more than its rendering parameters; the file was not changed", and previews laid out in a way that cannot be cleaned safely.

releases.name: Squint 0.9.3
releases.notes:
This release closes four gaps in Remove Location Data that the 0.9.2 review found but left for later.

GeoTIFF. A GeoTIFF's georeferencing survived a strip: tie points, pixel scale, transformation matrix and GeoKeys, and also RPC coefficients (whose offsets are the scene centre in degrees), the older Intergraph matrix and GDAL's metadata XML. All of them are now removed, as is a DNG preview's date. The picture is unchanged.

Raw files. A DNG keeps its raw image and previews in sub-directories, and their own tags were never read, so a camera, a date or an original file name written there stayed. Every sub-directory is now stripped, and its pixels are protected like any page's. A file whose directories overlap, or that names one directory in two roles, is refused rather than half stripped. On full-size Pentax and Nikon raws the sensor data comes back byte for byte.

Signed PDFs. A digitally signed PDF is now refused in every mode with its own message, because any change breaks the signature, which names the signer, the place and the time. A signature from an earlier revision that the document no longer uses is removed instead of refusing the file, and Reader's usage-rights signature,

releases.name: Squint 0.9.4
releases.notes:
This release closes ways in which Remove Location Data reported a raw file or TIFF clean while identifying data remained in it, found by a review of 0.9.3 against 176 real raw files.

Raw previews. A raw file carries an embedded preview, which is a JPEG with metadata of its own. An iPhone ProRAW file's preview keeps the GPS position, the phone, the lens and the capture time, and Remove Location Data removed everything else and reported the file clean. Such a file is now refused with its own message, "this file's embedded preview carries location or camera data that Strip cannot remove yet", and is not changed. A later release will clean the preview itself. Previews holding only what a decoder needs, as on most cameras, strip as before.

Samsung raw files. Samsung's NX cameras from 2014 on point their previews' resolution at the camera's name, model or capture date. Those bytes were left, most of the date included on an NX1. They are now removed; the resolution they shared is printing density, which no pixel depends on.

releases.name: Squint 0.9.2
releases.notes:
This release closes ways in which Remove Location Data left identifying metadata in a file while reporting it removed, found by two code audits and an outside review.

JPEG. A progressive JPEG may carry XMP or comment segments between its scans, and they survived; one holding a thumbnail could also cut the picture short. They are now removed and the scans kept whole. Adobe's colour-transform segment, which a CMYK JPEG needs to render with the right colours, is kept, and only when it is exactly that segment.

HDR gain maps. A gain map's own XMP was copied back whole, so a location written there survived. releases.notes:
Pepecoin-Qt 1.1.0 for macOS on Apple Silicon, built by CI from `2fa18e36`. The first release of this fork. The dmg is signed with a Developer ID (Benjamin Meadows, team CY9SLX2KFM) and notarized by Apple, so Gatekeeper opens it without a warning. Drag the app to your Applications folder before you open it.

Upstream Pepecoin Core has no Apple Silicon build, so this fork builds `Pepecoin-Qt` natively for arm64 (#1, #2). CI checks that the bundle is arm64, that its Berkeley DB version keeps `wallet.dat` compatible, and that it does not load a library from outside the bundle other than the system frameworks (#4).

SHA-256 of `Pepecoin-Qt-1.1.0-arm64.dmg`: `a44d5bfcf459e46b634cdf5ec92bb475b9a8d001e5d76280b083ee9b3c9514b4`

Remove Location Data on a HEIC now leaves a valid, empty EXIF block where the old one was. It used to fill that block with zeros. Pillow then refused the stripped file's metadata as "not a TIFF file", and on photographs from older iPhones the HDR range came out smaller: Apple keeps the strength of the gain map in two maker-note values inside EXIF, and without them Image I/O reported 3.48 of headroom where the original had 8.00 (iPhone 14 Pro Max), 6.91 (iPhone 15 Pro) and 4.00 (iPhone 12). The new block holds those two values and nothing else, so the location, camera and date are still removed and the headroom is unchanged. An XMP packet is kept only when everything in it describes the gain map or the segmentation matte. Any other XMP packet is emptied.

Remove Location Data on a file that has nothing to remove says so, and leaves the file alone. It used to report that the result would be no smaller than the original, which is the message for a size search. A second Remove Location Data on the same HEIC is now one of those cases.

releases.name: Emoji Fix 1.3.2
releases.notes:
Emoji Fix 1.3.2 draws emoji in rich-text editors whose content sets its own inline `font-family`. Outlook on the web wraps each compose paragraph in such a `<div>`, which overrides the font the extension sets on the editing host, so emoji typed or pasted into an Outlook message stayed blank. That content now gets a stylesheet rule matching its inline declaration, and the edited markup is still not changed. The README now links the Chrome Web Store listing.

Install from the Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/emoji-fix/pgjaolgpjogppmhdadddafkfcbnndeam

To install from this release, unzip `emoji-fix-1.3.2.zip`, open `brave://extensions`, turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and select the unzipped folder.

Requires Chromium 119 or later. SHA-256 of the zip: `ca9470d3cb058cec7854001c67c7840008634950674de3706ae1ebf136f641ad`.

releases.name: Emoji Fix 1.4.0
releases.notes:
Emoji Fix 1.4.0 adds a per-site off switch and stops running inside anti-bot challenge frames. In 1.3.2 its page script replaced a built-in browser function inside Cloudflare Turnstile's frame; Turnstile read that as tampering and failed verification. 1.4.0 skips the frames of Cloudflare Turnstile, hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA and Arkose Labs.

Click the toolbar button to turn Emoji Fix off or on for the current site. The tab reloads, and the button shows an "off" badge wherever it is off.

New permissions: `scripting` and `storage`. Access to all sites, which the content scripts already had, is now declared in `host_permissions`. The only stored data is the list of sites where it is off.

Install from the Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/emoji-fix/pgjaolgpjogppmhdadddafkfcbnndeam (the store copy updates to 1.4.0 after Google's review).

To install from this release, unzip `emoji-fix-1.4.0.zip`, open `brave://extensions`, turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and select the unzipped folder.

Requires Chromium 119 or later. SHA-256 of the zip: `50ebfa4838768a4c439f23c04e545864ee21128c4d847a3e1a71967406cb1417`.

releases.name: Emoji Fix 1.3.0
releases.notes:
Emoji Fix draws emoji with a bundled Noto Color Emoji font on Macs where Brave and other Chromium browsers draw Apple Color Emoji as blank space. It works on X, including the chat and the reaction picker.

To install, unzip `emoji-fix-1.3.0.zip`, open `brave://extensions`, turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and select the unzipped folder.

Changes since the first public commit (1.2.0), from a security and bug review recorded in `review/`:

- Flags, keycaps and skin-tone modifiers are detected. Text symbols such as the trademark sign and check marks are no longer replaced with emoji glyphs.
- In rich-text editors the font is set on the editing host, so the style does not enter the edited document.
- The fix survives element reuse by frameworks, page `!important` font rules and replacement of the page body, and covers inputs, SVG text, text directly in shadow roots, and `srcdoc` frames.
- The font loads through a per-session URL, so pages cannot probe for the extension by a fixed ID.
- The shadow-root hook returns the native result unchanged if its notification fails.

Requires Chromium 119 or later. SHA-256 of the zip: `60247efb588504e148924283ed2fe5cfd83a30727c714c27b821f

releases.name: v1.1.0
releases.notes: Theme release v1.1.0.

Shrink and Shrink to a Quality Target now keep an iPhone photograph's HDR gain map when they replace the file. Until now they dropped it and said so: the photograph still opened and looked right on an ordinary display, but it looked flat on the display it was taken for. macOS will only decode a gain map beside a picture its own encoder wrote, so for a photograph that has one, the system encoder writes the file and the map is copied across from the original. That costs about 30% more bytes than Squint's usual encoder at the same score, and it is used only when there is a map to keep. Measured on an iPhone 12 portrait: 3,995 KB to 1,505 KB with Shrink, the HDR headroom 4.00 before and after, and no location, camera or date left in the file.

Shrink for Email and Shrink for Social still drop the map. They make a smaller copy to send, and the original beside them keeps its range.

The window's picker now offers all six treatments the Finder entries do: Shrink, Email, Social, Quality, AVIF and Strip. A photo can be dropped on the window and sent through any of them, which matters in folders where Finder shows no Services entries.

Remove Location Data could stall on a hostile TIFF. A forty-byte file declaring an entry count in the billions made the directory walk run once per declared entry, which took tens of seconds, although every read past the end of the file failed. A second defect, in the same walker, let the engine's internal count of bytes destroyed exceed the size of the file when a directory chain looped back on itself; the application only uses that count to decide whether anything was removed, so nothing visible changed. Same code as 2.1.0 plus the in-app update check for this fork. Apple Silicon only; the bundle has an ad-hoc signature, so follow the Open Anyway steps in the README to open it.

- The update check reads this fork's latest GitHub release instead of upstream's version file, and Download Now opens that release's page. A user-initiated check that cannot reach the release list now says so.
- A 2.1.0 install still checks upstream, so it does not learn about this release from inside the application. Download it from the releases page.

The same Squint as 0.7.0, signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. It opens on first launch like any other application: no Privacy & Security detour, no **Open Anyway**.

Nothing in the engine or the application changed. The version exists because a signed and notarized build is a different set of bytes from the one already published as 0.7.0, whose archives, hashes and update signature stay exactly as they were.

What the signature covers: the application, the Sparkle framework, and each of the five pieces nested inside it — the two XPC services, `Autoupdate`, `Updater.app` and the framework binary — every one signed individually with the hardened runtime and a timestamp, then verified as a whole before submission. The notary ticket is stapled to the bundle, so Gatekeeper's answer does not depend on reaching Apple.

This is also the first update Sparkle delivers across a change of signing identity. Every earlier build was ad-hoc signed; this one carries a team. Sparkle permits that transition when the update's EdDSA signature is intact, which it is — the same key has signed every archive since 0.4.0. The build stays marked pre-release until an installed 0.6.0 or 0.7.0 ha

Two things the command line could do reach the Finder menu.

**A PDF goes through Shrink and Shrink to a Quality Target.** The pictures inside it are re-encoded, any above 150 dpi on the page are downscaled to it, the document's own record of who wrote it and with what is dropped, and the file is rewritten in place. A fax-coded page, a JPEG 2000 image or a CMYK image inside it is left exactly as it was. Measured on a 665 KB PDF wrapping one photograph: 124 KB through Shrink, 165 KB through the quality target.

**Squint: Convert to AVIF** is a new entry. It takes a JPEG, PNG, HEIC, WebP or SVG and writes `name.avif` beside it, at the picture's own size, searched to the quality target the way the Quality entry is; the original is not touched. Measured: a 662 KB JPEG became a 262 KB AVIF, a 7.8 MB PNG a 506 KB one, a 340 KB HEIC a 108 KB one, all at their source dimensions. An AVIF handed to it is refused rather than written over.

The C interface gains `squint_optimize_as`, which names the output format; a code it does not know is refused rather than read as JPEG. The application now decides from the bytes of a result, not from what was asked for, whether it may replace the original:

A row in the window now moves to its result the moment the work finishes.

Through 0.8.0 a row showed "working" after its file was done, and kept showing it until another file was added. The list drew each row from a plain reference to its job, so it redrew when a job was added or cleared but not when a job's own state changed. Each row now observes its job. Verified through the Finder path: one JPEG through Shrink, nothing else added, and the row read its result as soon as the file was written.

The drop prompt names PDF, which the in-place modes have accepted since 0.8.0.

releases.name: FreeWallet 2.1.0
releases.notes:
First release of the fork. Apple Silicon only. The bundle has an ad-hoc signature, so follow the Open Anyway steps in the README to open it.

### Wallet encryption

- The wallet is encrypted at rest with a PBKDF2-derived key (SHA-256, 310,000 iterations, per-wallet salt) and a stored verifier. The password itself is no longer stored in any form. The previous format derived its key with one round of MD5 and kept the password beside the ciphertext, which allowed an offline guess-check with no work factor.
- A wallet password is required. A new or changed password must have at least 12 characters, including a number.
- An existing wallet is re-encrypted the first time it is unlocked after installing this build. A wallet that already had a password keeps it, even a shorter one. A wallet that had none must choose one. The previous copy is retained until that unlock succeeds, and if the re-encrypted copy is damaged before then, the wallet is rebuilt from the retained copy.
- The password can be changed under Settings, on the Wallet tab. The change asks for the current password.
- The application never opens a wallet without the password, and a damaged wallet record can no longer lead to

siteWeeks.title: Prayers now print cleanly on paper
siteWeeks.summary: Printed services now come out in black on white with red rubrics, book-style paragraphs, page numbers and no screen controls, and prayers no longer split awkwardly.

siteWeeks.title: ENS names resolve on the new registry
siteWeeks.summary: ENS names, including names migrated to the new registry and Base names, now resolve correctly, with clearer messages when a name cannot be found.

siteWeeks.title: Credential links to public license registries
siteWeeks.summary: Two plumbing credentials, the Arizona contractor license and the Texas journeyman license, now link to the public registries that confirm them.

siteWeeks.title: Country filter, mint counts and description search
siteWeeks.summary: The archive now covers drops through October 2026, with a country filter, a most-minted sort, mint counts, typo-tolerant search and description search.

siteWeeks.title: Twelve September 2026 drops added to archive
siteWeeks.summary: The archive now holds 197,589 events, including twelve September 2026 drops, with artwork and metadata served from new October roots.

siteWeeks.title: The Typika added
siteWeeks.summary: The Typika now has its own page, set word for word from a printed Reader's Service booklet, with the Beatitudes and Psalm 33 in Hapgood's translation.

siteWeeks.title: Talk recordings streamed and image loading restored
siteWeeks.summary: Recordings from the speaking archive can now be streamed and seeked, and POAP images load again after two public IPFS gateways stopped working.

siteWeeks.title: Compline, Communion prayers and evening rule added
siteWeeks.summary: The full evening rule, Compline, the Three Canons, and the prayers before and after Holy Communion are now on the site, with grouped contents.

siteWeeks.title: Random icon on the Not Found page
siteWeeks.summary: The Not Found page now shows one of fourteen spot illustrations, crosses, stars and a seraph, chosen at random on each visit, and the app icon has been redrawn.

siteWeeks.title: Archive grows by 7,424 recovered events
siteWeeks.summary: The archive now holds 197,577 events after a crawl past the old ceiling, and the browsing grid loads small thumbnails instead of full originals.

siteWeeks.title: Full morning rule and evening prayers added
siteWeeks.summary: The complete morning rule now has its own page, joined by evening prayers, table prayers, the Commemoration, and the prayers after every kathisma.

siteWeeks.title: Browsable gallery and event lookup added
siteWeeks.summary: Rescued badges now appear in a browsable gallery, events can be looked up by ID with download links, and a readout shows which events the archive covers.
